facts.claim: Manipulated photos were rated more positively than original photos, even though the reshaping of the bodies was not noticed very well.
facts.quote: Interestingly, the manipulated photos were rated more positively than the original photos. Although the use of filters and effects was detected, reshaping of the bodies was not noticed very well.

facts.claim: Exposure to manipulated Instagram photos directly leads to lower body image in girls aged 14–18.
facts.quote: Results showed that exposure to manipulated Instagram photos directly led to lower body image.

facts.claim: Girls with higher social comparison tendencies are negatively affected by exposure to manipulated photos.
facts.quote: Especially, girls with higher social comparison tendencies were negatively affected by exposure to the manipulated photos.

facts.claim: Body image was significantly more negative after viewing thin media images than after viewing images of either average size models, plus size models, or inanimate objects.
facts.quote: Body image was significantly more negative after viewing thin media images than after viewing images of either average size models, plus size models, or inanimate objects.

facts.claim: The negative effect of thin media images on body image was stronger for participants less than 19 years of age.
facts.quote: This effect was stronger for between-subjects designs, participants less than 19 years of age, and for participants who are vulnerable to activation of a thinness schema.

facts.claim: Internalization of body shape ideals is strongly linked to body dissatisfaction in younger individuals.
facts.quote: IBSI and body dissatisfaction were strongly linked: (a) in younger individuals (general attractiveness-ideal internalization);

rejected.claim: Upward social comparison on social media causes a negative effect on body image with an effect size of g = −0. 31.
rejected.quote: Specifically, there were significant negative effects of upward comparison on each outcome variable: body image (g = −0. 31, p < . 001)

research.angle: Viewing idealized and manipulated images on social media causes lower body satisfaction, particularly for younger people with a tendency to compare themselves to others.
research.verdict: The evidence consistently shows that exposure to thin or manipulated beauty ideals on social media leads to lower body satisfaction, especially among adolescents.
research.caveat: While body-positive content shows promise in improving mood and satisfaction in the short term, its influence on social comparison remains limited.
